summary: Phase 4 Step 4 (Admin Fund Requests) tested end-to-end. Backend: 25/25 pytest passed in /app/backend/tests/test_admin_phase4_step4_fund_requests.py — RBAC (401 anon, 403 agent) on GET list / GET detail / POST create / POST approve / POST reject; list shape returns fund_requests[] + pending_count + page/page_size/total; status filter pending|approved|rejected all constrain rows to that status; bad status value → 422; POST /api/admin/fund-requests creates pending row on behalf of agent (amount 250 verified via GET); amount 99.99 → 400, amount 1_000_000.01 → 400, unknown agent_id → 404; approve credits booking_balance by exact amount (₱777 delta observed), writes TOP_UP txn with idempotency_key='fund_request:{id}', flips status→approved, detail endpoint returns transaction snapshot with type=top_up; second approve on same id returns already_approved=true with same transaction_id and balance did NOT drift (Decimal equality); rejecting an approved request → 409; reject with 'insufficient proof' (17 chars) → 200 rejected + no txn on detail; reject with 'no' (2 chars) → 400/422; rejecting an already-rejected request → 409; approving a rejected request → 409. Regression smoke: /api/admin/agents, /api/admin/bookings, /api/admin/packages, /api/public/packages all 200. Frontend (Playwright, admin session): sidebar shows 'Fund Requests' entry (no 'Approvals SOON'); /admin/fund-requests renders admin-fund-requests-tabs with All/Pending/Approved/Rejected filters, all clickable; 'New request' opens admin-fund-request-create-dialog with 2 agents in picker (Demo Agent + Disable Test); created ₱333 UI-REF-A row, then approved it — toast shown 'Approved — new booking balance ₱3,333' and row appeared in Approved tab (5 approved rows now including newest). Dashboard KPI 'Pending approvals' card links to /admin/fund-requests?status=pending as required. Recent activity feed on dashboard shows fund_request.approve / fund_request.reject / fund_request.create_on_behalf audit entries with fresh timestamps, confirming audit_logs are being written by all three write paths. No defects found.
critical_code_review_comments: financial_service.approve_fund_request: the idempotency short-circuit returns fr.get('status') from the freshly-fetched fund_request doc, which may still be 'pending' if a prior partial write left the request in that state (transaction inserted but fund_request update failed). Recommend refetching or explicitly returning 'approved' since we know a TOP_UP txn exists. Not observed in this run, but worth hardening.

financial_service.approve_fund_request: sequential writes (txn insert → profile update → fund_request update → audit) without a Mongo transaction. On stand-alone dev servers this is acceptable per module docstring, but crashes between steps could leave: balance credited + txn written but fund_request still 'pending'. A next-idempotent-call would then see the existing txn (short-circuit) and NOT flip status to approved. Consider making the short-circuit branch also flip the status if fund_request is still pending — that would fully self-heal.

admin_fund_requests.CreateFundRequestIn.amount uses Pydantic Field(gt=0) — an amount of '0.01' would pass Pydantic then fail the MIN_AMOUNT<=100 check in code with a 400. This is correct behaviour; just noting the two-layer validation.

admin_fund_requests.list_fund_requests emits pending_count regardless of the applied status filter (nice for the KPI). Consider also emitting approved_count and rejected_count so the sidebar/tab badges do not each require a separate query.

admin_fund_requests.get_fund_request eagerly loads the linked transaction but not the deciding admin user. When the UI wants to show 'approved by X 2m ago', it currently must resolve the admin from decided_by_user_id via a separate call.

AdminFundRequestsPage reject dialog: the create dialog's amount input accepts any string — no client-side inline validation for min 100 / max 1_000_000, so the user only learns via the server 400 toast. Minor UX polish.

AdminFundRequestsPage does not appear to disable the Approve button while the approve mutation is in flight, so a rapid double-click could send two requests concurrently. Backend is idempotent so no double-credit, but the UI could be tighter (disable during pending).
